subject: Model fit evals & parity - next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@paygrid.com>; Samir Patel <samir.patel@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit evals

Hi Emily / Samir —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + model-fit discussion and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Top customer needs (from call): fast, deterministic invoice parsing + classification; low hallucination tolerance; on-prem option for PII-sensitive workloads.
- Success criteria we agreed on: >=95% intent/field-extraction accuracy for core invoice fields; <2% regression vs your current proprietary baseline on downstream match-rate; production latency target 150ms p50 for API inference under expected QPS.
- Models we recommend starting with for the eval:
  - Open candidate: Mistral-7B + Redwood-tokenization prompt set (smaller size, strong cost profile)
  - Open candidate: Llama-2-13B (quantized) — good middle ground for accuracy/cost
  - Proprietary baseline for parity: redwood-pro-base-1.2 (we’ll run head-to-head)

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
1) We’ll upload a starter prompt set + suggested eval harness to a shared Drive (Marissa) — today EOD.
2) PayGrid to share a small sample of redacted invoices and target metrics (Samir) — ideally by Thu 3/5.
3) Redwood to run an initial benchmark (Marissa + Aditya) against the sample and report back with a parity scorecard — target Mon 3/9.
4) If open models hit acceptance thresholds, we’ll propose a canary rollout plan for dedicated capacity and a cost estimate (Lauren).

Attachments I’ll include: our recommended prompt set CSV and a compressed results template you can re-run locally.

Questions before we proceed?

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit evals

Thanks, Lauren — this looks great and aligned with what we discussed. A couple quick items from our side: 

- We can share a redacted sample set (~500 invoices) by end of day Thu (3/5). I'll have our data engineer attach the file to the Drive link you provide.
- For parity: we currently measure extraction F1 and downstream reconciliation match-rate. The match-rate is most important for procurement; if an open model is within 1-2 percentage points of our baseline on match-rate and doesn't introduce additional false positives, we can consider it acceptable for a pilot.
- One ask: can you include latency percentiles (p50/p95) and token-level cost estimates in the initial report? That's a key tradeoff for our infra team.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here.

Best,
Emily Ross
Head of Integrations, PayGrid
emily.ross@paygrid.com
(617) 555-8822

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@paygrid.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@paygrid.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit evals

Emily / Samir —

Uploading the starter artifacts to the shared drive now: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/paygrid/evals/2026-03-v1.

Included:
- paygrid_eval_prompts.csv (seed prompts + instruction templates)
- paygrid_bench_results_v1.pdf (blank results template + examples)
- runbook.md (short instructions for running the harness locally or in our hosted sandbox)

Quick notes on our benchmarking approach:
- We’ll run Llama-2-13B (int8 quantized) and Mistral-7B (int8) as the open-model candidates.
- Baseline is redwood-pro-base-1.2 (your current vendor-equivalent run configured to match your latency targets).
- Metrics reported: extraction F1, reconciliation match-rate, p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-invoice, and estimated $/1k invoices.
- Acceptance thresholds we’ll flag in the scorecard: >=95% extraction F1 AND match-rate within -2 percentage points of baseline. If both hold, we mark parity = yes.

Note on quality regressions: we’ll include prompt-sensitivity tests (10% prompt variation) and a small adversarial set to measure hallucination risk. If a candidate shows >3% drop on adversarials vs baseline, we’ll call out a regression risk even if nominal metrics look okay.

Planned deliverable: initial benchmark PDF + parity scorecard by Mon 3/9 (Marissa / Aditya). If we need more compute or a private VPC run for the proprietary baseline, we’ll flag it in the report and propose a short SOW.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Ross <emily.ross@paygrid.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — model fit evals (internal summary)

Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for getting the artifacts up. Quick internal alignment before the benchmark run:

- Prioritization: start with Mistral-7B single-run + Llama-2-13B as a secondary. Mistral tends to be cost-friendly and often strong on extraction tasks.
- Acceptance gating: we’ll require BOTH criteria to mark parity — (1) extraction F1 >=95% and (2) match-rate within -2pp of redwood-pro-base-1.2. If only one criterion is met, mark as 'partial parity' and include notes about likely remediation (prompt engineering / light finetune).
- Latency/cost: include p50/p95 and a rough $/1k invoice estimate; flag if p95 > 300ms even if p50 is fine.
- Risk callouts: any model that shows >3% adversarial degradation or any consistent hallucination on line-item totals should be escalated to the product risk board before pilot.

Action: Marissa to kick off hosted run today; Aditya to instrument token-cost calc and p95 timing hooks. I’ll draft a short decision memo we can use in the SLA conversation with PayGrid if parity is achieved.

Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
